meta.title: Throne — Memory and task framing for humans
meta.description: Throne is a local memory and task-framing layer for people working with AI agents. Persistent context, intents, instructions, and MCP routing.
meta.ogAlt: Throne — Memory and task framing for humans

hero.title: Keep context across tasks, agents, and conversations
hero.subtitle: Throne turns scattered requests, ideas, and preferences into working units. You switch between tasks, and agents pick up fresh context without manual retelling.

theory.title: The productive AI work loop
theory.body: The interview unpacks the intent. Work delivers the result. The knowledge base captures context and feeds it back into the next pass — into the new interview and the new work.
theory.tagline: Throne is that knowledge base with an MCP interface. A path to interviews and code work in any agent stack.

video.title: Throne in five minutes
video.body: A short walkthrough: creating an Intent, handing it to an agent over MCP, and improving the result through patches.

features.title: Context under your control
features.subtitle: Throne gives a clean interface for working with intents, links, and instructions. Agents don't have to keep everything in a single chat — they fetch and update context through MCP.

items.title: Intent workspace
items.text: Every task lives as an Intent: a wording, history, links, questions, and work results. Context no longer scatters across chats.

items.title: Links between tasks
items.text: Connect Intents to each other: continuation, dependency, refinement, bug, fix. The agent sees a map of work, not an isolated request.

items.title: MCP for every operation
items.text: Any agent can read, create, and update Intents, attach questions, capture reviews, and pull instructions through the MCP interface.

items.title: Your personal skill in the cloud
items.text: It's your personal skill in the cloud: rules, style, and preferences apply automatically when the agent starts an interview or a work session.

items.title: Dream retrospective
items.text: Ask your agent to review past conversations and propose a patch to your instructions. You accept or reject the change — memory improves transparently.

items.title: UX for the human
items.text: Throne shows what context a task has, which instructions the agent will receive, and what changed after the work. Memory management stays visible.

connect.title: Three steps to your first Intent
connect.intro: Throne runs locally. Embedded terminal is the primary path; standalone clients connect directly to http://localhost:5008/mcp as a secondary path.

run.title: Run Throne locally
run.description: API + UI + Mongo in one command. UI at http://localhost:8080, API at http://localhost:5008.
run.snippet:
git clone https://github.com/gently-whitesnow/throne
cd throne
docker compose --profile full up --build -d

embedded.title: Use embedded first
embedded.description: In host-backend mode Throne starts the agent from the UI, injects context upfront, and tracks lifecycle through hooks. This is more reliable than relying on standalone MCP routing hints.

connect.clientsDescription: Use this when the agent runs outside the Throne UI. Ask the agent explicitly to work through Throne; the mini-router is a best-effort hint.

claudeDesktop.label: Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.description: Use the standard mcp-remote stdio to HTTP bridge. Plain HTTP localhost requires --allow-http; if local policy blocks it, prefer embedded terminal or Claude Code CLI.

claudeCode.label: Claude Code
claudeCode.description: CLI: claude mcp add --transport http throne http://localhost:5008/mcp · manual: ~/.claude.json (mcpServers).

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.description: macOS/Linux: ~/.cursor/mcp.json · Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json. Reconnect from settings if HTTP keep-alive drops.

codex.label: Codex
codex.description: CLI: codex mcp add throne --url http://localhost:5008/mcp · manual: ~/.codex/config.toml.

roadmap.title: Where Throne is heading
roadmap.intro: The core loop: brief the agent, give it context, verify the result, and keep useful takeaways for the next run. Each direction below strengthens one of these steps.

items.title: Easier verification
items.text: Diffs, change history, static analysis, diagrams. The goal — see faster what the agent got right and where another pass is needed.

items.title: Connecting work systems
items.text: Bug reports, task managers, messengers, and internal knowledge bases. Throne pulls in incoming context and turns it into an Intent.

items.title: Intermediate task memory
items.text: Steps, partial solutions, open questions, dependencies, and state across multiple agent passes.

items.title: Long-lived project context
items.text: Architectural decisions, repo rules, team conventions, and recurring patterns. The agent gets personal plus project-specific context.

items.title: Workspaces for teams
items.text: Roles, shared instructions, project memory, intent history, and access control. Throne becomes a team-level loop for working with agents.

contacts.title: Reach the author
contacts.body: Throne is run by a single author. Open channels — GitHub and Telegram.

footer.tagline: Memory and task framing for humans
